slides.headline: Two fans. Very different jobs.
slides.subline: Choose by duct length and resistance, not by the price tag.

slides.title: Axial fan: air goes straight through
slides.intro: The blades push air in the direction it is already travelling.

items.title: Best on short runs
items.text: A direct discharge through a wall or a short roof duct.

items.title: Moves a lot, pushes little
items.text: Good volume at low resistance, and it suffers as filters load.

items.title: Simple and compact
items.text: Fewer moving parts and a clear straight path for the air.

slides.title: Centrifugal fan: turned, then driven
slides.intro: Air enters at the centre, leaves under pressure.

items.title: Best on longer ductwork
items.text: Keeps pulling where a straight fan would fall away.

items.title: Holds up against resistance
items.text: Bends, filters and long runs add load. This copes.

items.title: Easier on the ear
items.text: Less rush at the outlet, easier above a kitchen.

slides.note_text: Both are roof-mounted. The route picks the type.

slides.headline: Not sure which fan your duct needs?
slides.subline: Send the route and we will size it.

caption_en:
Axial or centrifugal? The real question is which duct you have, not which fan is better.

Axial fans push air straight through and suit short, direct runs with little resistance. Centrifugal fans draw air in and drive it out under pressure, so they keep pulling against long ductwork, bends and loaded filters.

Choosing by price alone usually means choosing twice. Send us your duct route and we will match the fan to it, roof-mounted and installed by our own team in Doha.
